headline: Highest risk is medium: Great Expectations can read and write validation files while awesome-nlp is a non-runnable docs-only list, so interaction risks are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default instruction-ingestion path is shown. agent_a is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces; agent_b exposes files for data sources and validation results, but nothing indicates it consumes agent_a output as instructions. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so prompt injection is not evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a is later wired to emit text into a file that agent_b parses as instructions, the risk changes.
IF a shared clipboard, queue, or MCP bridge is added between them, reassess as higher severity.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared folders.
Do not feed agent_a-generated text into agent_b parsers.
Add provenance labels to any exchanged files.
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation on any inter-agent text handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and has no network egress, while agent_b handles validation results and documentation with file I/O but also has no egress. Without a shared workspace or sensitive data class, leakage blast radius is small and the pathway is not defaulted.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF agent_b is pointed at regulated data sources, its file outputs may expose those contents.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Restrict agent_b to non-sensitive sample datasets.
Review validation-result files before sharing them.
Delete temporary outputs after each run.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write or runtime capabilities exposed, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. agent_b can install packages and write files, but without a second writer or shared mutable target, conflict is limited to unusual orchestration setups.
conditions: IF agent_a is replaced with a writable runtime, overlapping writes could emerge.
IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or environment, package/file conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Run them in separate environments.
Avoid sharing writable directories.
Pin package versions for agent_b.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b can consume validation results and documentation, but agent_a is only an awesome-list repository and is not runnable, so there is no strong default chain where agent_a produces authoritative facts that agent_b acts on. The main risk is manual misuse of list content, not an automated cascade.
conditions: IF agent_a content is manually copied into agent_b as authoritative configuration, downstream errors can cascade.
IF agent_b is configured to auto-ingest external documentation without review, the risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review before using agent_a content.
Keep agent_b inputs limited to vetted sources.
Annotate imported references with source URLs.
requires-engineering: add verification checks before acting on imported facts.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced. agent_a touches no data classes and agent_b lists documentation, validation results, and data-quality tests only; neither profile shows PHI, EU PII, residency constraints, or retention differences. With only docs-only evidence, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into agent_b's validation inputs, reassess residency and retention controls.
IF either agent is later assigned PHI or EU PII, compliance analysis must be redone.
mitigations: Confirm no regulated data is in scope.
Document retention for validation outputs.
Separate test data from production data.
requires-engineering: add policy checks for regulated datasets.
